sourcedFrom: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The RXD22Ti is a rimfire can and it comes apart in a way that will surprise you: the CORE unscrews out of the TUBE, and the Front Cap Ring at the front is LEFT-HAND threaded — you turn it CLOCKWISE to take it off. ⛔ It is rated for .22 WMR and 5.7x28 and optimised for .22 LR, and Dead Air says in capitals that it is NOT rated for 5.56 NATO even though the 1/2-28 thread will screw straight onto one.

steps.title: Host clear, and the can does not go on a closed action
steps.action: Magazine out, action open, chamber checked. Dead Air refers you to your own firearm's manual for the clearing procedure, then rules out installing on a closed action.
steps.prose: Rimfire hosts are the ones people are casual with. The rule is the same.
steps.quote: CHECK YOUR FIREARM’S CHAMBER AND MAKE CERTAIN THAT THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND THE MAGAZINE REMOVED BEFORE PROCEEDING ANY FURTHER. IF THERE IS ANY QUESTION OR DOUBT, CONSULT THE OWNER’S MANUAL APPLICABLE TO YOUR FIREARM AS TO THE PROPER PROCEDURE FOR CLEARING AND/OR UNLOADING YOUR FIREARM.
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — General Considerations, p.4
steps.warn: DO NOT INSTALL YOUR NEW SUPPRESSOR ON A FIREARM WITH A CLOSED ACTION!

steps.title: ⛔ 1/2-28 fits a 5.56 rifle. The RXD22Ti is not rated for one
steps.action: Before anything else, confirm what this can has been on. Dead Air rates it for .22 Winchester Magnum Rimfire and 5.7x28mm, optimised for .22 LR, and states plainly that it is NOT rated for 5.56 NATO — the thread pitch matching is not permission.
steps.prose: This is the single most consequential sentence in the book, and it exists because the mistake is easy to make.
steps.quote: THE RXD22TI IS NOT RATED FOR 5.56 NATO. IT IS ONLY RATED FOR CALIBERS LISTED IN THIS MANUAL. EVEN THOUGH THE THREAD PITCH IS COMPATIBLE WITH RIFLES CHAMBERED IN 5.56 NATO AND OTHER CARTRIDGES WITH A HIGHER CHAMBER PRESSURES, IT IS RATED UP TO .22 WINCHESTER MAGNUM RIMFIRE AND 5.7X28MM, NOT .223 REM/5.56 NATO.
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Installation Notes, p.6
steps.warn: THE SUPPRESSOR MAY BECOME EXTREMELY HOT AFTER USE. NEVER GRAB A HOT SUPPRESSOR AS IT CAN RESULT IN BURNS AND INJURY.

steps.title: Off the XRF mount — and the tube may back off the core instead
steps.action: Rotate the can counter-clockwise off the XRF muzzle device. With the supplied tools, put the larger open-ended core wrench on the CORE and turn counter-clockwise, then finish by hand. ⚠ Without tools the TUBE can unscrew from the CORE first instead — Dead Air says that is normal and to be expected if the mount was over-torqued.
steps.prose: You end up holding a tube in one hand and a core still on the rifle. Nothing is broken; keep going and unscrew the core from the mount.
steps.quote: There is a possibility that the tube will back off the core. This is normal and to be expected if too much torque was applied to the XRF mount when mounting the suppressor.
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Suppressor Installation and Removal — Removal without Tools, p.7

steps.title: ⛔ The Front Cap Ring is LEFT-HAND — turn it CLOCKWISE to remove
steps.action: The Front Cap Ring ships fitted and normally stays fitted. For cleaning it comes off with the supplied tools, or by laying a 3/32 Allen wrench across the grooves and turning CLOCKWISE. Left-hand threads: every instinct you have about which way to turn is backwards here.
steps.prose: Forcing it counter-clockwise tightens it. That is how a ring gets galled onto a titanium tube.
steps.caution: Left-hand thread. Clockwise OFF, counter-clockwise ON.
steps.quote: The threads on the Front Cap Ring are left-hand threads. In the event of cleaning, the Front Cap Ring can be removed by using the supplied tools or by laying a 3/32 Allen wrench across the groves on the Front Cap Ring and with a clockwise motion turn the Front Cap Ring off.
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Front Cap Ring Installation and Removal, p.7

steps.title: Control surfaces: threads, tapers, every mating face
steps.action: Get the control surfaces clean — threads, taper surfaces and all mating surfaces. Where there is build-up, a nylon or brass brush with cleaning oil, lightly, until it is gone. Then wipe the excess off with a shop or paper towel.
steps.prose: "Lightly" is the operative word. These surfaces are the alignment.
steps.caution: Caustic or acidic chemicals discolor Nitride and PVD and strip Cerakote.
steps.quote: STEP TWO: MUZZLE DEVICE, FRONT CAP RING, AND SUPPRESSOR CONTROL SURFACES Ensure control surfaces such as threads, taper surfaces, and all mating surfaces, are clean of any debris. If debris or build-up is present, using a nylon or brass brush and cleaning oil, lightly brush the surfaces until the build-up or debris is removed.
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Suppressor Cleaning and Maintenance, Step Two, p.9

steps.title: Rimfire fouling: solvent and ultrasonic, no heat, no aluminium
steps.action: Clean the internal body with commercially available non-toxic, water-soluble, biodegradable solutions. An ultrasonic tank WITHOUT heat and WITHOUT corrosive chemicals may be used on titanium, steel or Haynes. ⛔ Never put aluminium in an ultrasonic tank.
steps.prose: A .22 can fills with wax and lead faster than any centrefire. This is the process that actually shifts it.
steps.quote: To enhance cleaning of the internal surfaces and geometry an ultra-sonic tank WITHOUT HEAT AND/OR CORROSIVE CHEMICALS may be used on any materials such as Titanium, Steel, or Haynes.
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Suppressor Cleaning and Maintenance, Step Three, p.9
steps.warn: NEVER USE ULTRA-SONIC TANKS AND ALUMINUM.

steps.title: ⛔ Front Cap Ring onto the TUBE FIRST, then the core — 50 in-lb
steps.action: Order matters and Dead Air prints it in capitals: if the Front Cap Ring was ever removed, it goes back onto the TUBE BEFORE the CORE goes in. Torque it to 50 inch-pounds. Then insert the core back into the tube and tighten the core back to the tube.
steps.prose: Put the core in first and the ring has nowhere to land. It is the one assembly order in this book that is written in capitals.
steps.quote: NOTE: IF THE FRONT CAP RING IS EVER REMOVED ENSURE THAT IT IS INSTALLED ON THE TUBE FIRST BEFORE INSTALLING THE CORE. TORQUE TO 50 INCH-POUNDS
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Front Cap Ring Installation and Removal, p.7

steps.title: Snug, no gaps, no rattle
steps.action: Everything should be snug with no gaps or rattling. If a component is not fully tightened, check the threads for damage or debris, clean both mating parts and repeat the tightening step.
steps.prose: A rattle in a rimfire can is usually a loose core, and a loose core is a strike.
steps.quote: All components should be snug with no gaps or rattling. If any component is not fully tightened, then check threads for any damage or debris. Clean both mating parts as necessary and repeat the tightening step.
steps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Inspection Upon Assembly, p.8

deepSteps.title: Direct-thread conversion — the XRF mount torqued INTO the core
deepSteps.action: The RXD22Ti can be made a direct-thread-only can: torque the XRF muzzle device INTO the suppressor core, with a 1-1/16 inch, 27 mm and 3/4 inch wrench or the supplied tools, to 15 foot-pounds. Onto a barrel the same device goes to 20 foot-pounds.
deepSteps.prose: Two different figures for the same part depending on which end it is screwed into. Worth writing on the box.
deepSteps.quote: Note: The RXD22Ti is designed such that if you want to have a direct thread only suppressor you may torque the XRF muzzle device into the suppressor core with a 1-1/16”, 27mm, and 3/4” wrench or the supplied tools, to 15 foot-pounds.
deepSteps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Muzzle Device Installation, p.6

deepSteps.title: If the mount keeps loosening, it is a thread-locker problem
deepSteps.action: Heavy heat cycles can walk the mount loose on the barrel. Dead Air's answer is to degrease the threads and use a MEDIUM-strength, high-temperature thread locker — it names Vibra-Tite 123 — rather than a high-strength one that will need heat to undo.
deepSteps.prose: High-strength locker on a suppressor mount is a trap: getting it off later needs the heat you are told not to apply.
deepSteps.quote: Dead Air recommends using a medium-strength, high temperature thread locker like Vibra-Tite 123 for average operating conditions.
deepSteps.cite: RXD22Ti .22 CALIBER TITANIUM SUPPRESSOR OWNER’S MANUAL — Rev061125 — Installation Notes, p.6

cleaning.name: CORE, TUBE AND FRONT CAP RING
tasks: Core unscrewed from the tube for access
Front Cap Ring off CLOCKWISE — left-hand thread — with a 3/32 Allen wrench
Ring back on the TUBE first, 50 inch-pounds, before the core returns

cleaning.name: CONTROL SURFACES
tasks: Threads, tapers and mating faces brushed lightly with nylon or brass and oil
Excess wiped off with a shop or paper towel
No caustic or acidic chemicals near Nitride, PVD or Cerakote

cleaning.name: MAIN BODY
tasks: Ultrasonic WITHOUT heat and WITHOUT corrosive chemicals
⛔ No aluminium in the ultrasonic tank

reassembly: ⛔ Front Cap Ring onto the TUBE first — left-hand thread, counter-clockwise ON — 50 in-lb.
Core threaded back into the tube and tightened to the tube.
XRF mount onto the barrel at 20 ft-lb, or into the core at 15 ft-lb for direct thread.
Suppressor onto the XRF taper — light hand pressure is the whole torque spec.
Snug everywhere, no gaps, no rattle.
fncheck: Confirm the caliber first — .22 WMR / 5.7x28 rated, .22 LR optimised, ⛔ NOT 5.56 NATO. Then check the assembly by hand: core tight in the tube, Front Cap Ring seated, the can solid on the XRF mount with no rotation or wobble. If the XRF mount will not thread smoothly onto the firearm, or the core will not thread smoothly onto the mount, STOP — Dead Air's instruction is to halt to avoid thread damage and call customer service.
